A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HVM research. Their complete main texts, figures, table, algorithms, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.11 support comparison, including content relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original model simulations, BabyLM compression results, LLM evaluations, and analyses relating model likelihoods to previously collected human recall data.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds Llama 3 transfer evaluations in Figure 5.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same generative procedure, hierarchical parsing, chunk and variable proposals, forgetting, and representation cleaning. The revised explanations do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic hierarchical sequences, the same four BabyLM domains—CHILDES, BNC, Gutenberg, and Open Subtitles—and the same sequence recall and transfer task. The added Llama 3 models are evaluated within this existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 5 adds Llama 3 8B and 70B alongside GPT-2, Llama 2 7B/13B/70B, and the retained cognitive models. This is a limited comparator expansion; Appendix Figure 10 retains only the original comparator set.

E3.justification: The added Llama 3 evaluations introduce an 8B configuration alongside 70B, extending the previously evaluated Llama sizes of 7B, 13B, and 70B. Existing data sampling, trial structure, prompt-chaining procedure, metrics, and cognitive-model settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The hierarchical-memory comparison, abstraction-depth analysis, and human-fit regressions in Figures 3, 4, 6, and 10 are retained. The new Llama 3 bars extend the principal comparison without adding a distinct ablation, robustness test, or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Existing error-bar reporting and correlation statistics are unchanged. The Llama 3 bars use the existing reporting style; no new run counts, seed information, uncertainty definitions, or significance-testing procedures are supplied.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds control-group and variable-group transfer NLL results for Llama 3 8B and 70B, showing lower variable-group means, particularly for 8B. Table 1 and the existing results in Figures 3, 4, 5, 6, and 10 are retained.

T1.justification: v2 removes Section 3's O(PQ) complexity assertion for variable proposal. Theorems 1–3, their proofs, and the appendix definitions and mathematical derivations otherwise remain unchanged; the shortened non-identifiability discussion does not introduce a new proof.

C1.justification: The introduction drops the explicit claim that LLMs rely more on associative learning than abstraction. The main HVM contributions and the abstract's human-versus-LLM transfer claim remain, as does Section 4.4's group-comparison conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly identifies an expressivity limitation: HVM cannot capture two chunks separated by a variable number of chunks. It also interprets learning-order dependence through human curriculum learning and proposes using HVM for tokenization with transformers or state-space models.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future anonymous repository link for reviewers; v2's Reproducibility Statement provides a repository hyperlink and states that code is available. This improves documented access information, without adding substantial implementation, hardware, or hyperparameter details.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially broadens research positioning through explicit comparisons with DreamCoder, hierarchical Bayesian language and topic models, context-tree methods, the Helmholtz Machine, and CSCG. Developmental-learning references are also added, while the Chiang lossy-compression framing is removed.

P1.justification: The introduction, LLM motivation, related work, and discussion receive prose edits; Appendix A.3 is condensed. An explanatory paragraph moves from Section 2 to A.2, and the standalone Conclusion is removed, while the main methods/results sequence and appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 5 expands from eight to ten panels and standardizes the human-group label to Control. Figures 7 and 8 receive cosmetic cleanup, Figure 6's caption is clarified, and figures and Table 1 are repositioned; most graphical content remains identical.

improvement.justification: The added Llama 3 comparisons, explicit expressivity limitation, broader research positioning, and concrete code-access link provide useful incremental improvements. Reporting is incompletely updated: Section 4.4 still says four LLMs despite showing six, and Appendix A.11's purportedly all-model regression figure excludes the new Llama 3 models. These inconsistencies temper the gains.
